title: Mini quant lab notes: 4-bit runs & KV caching quick log
content:
Goal: quick record of micro-experiments with 4-bit quantized LLaMA-variant, KV cache behavior, and prompt abrasive tests. Not exhaustive — quick notes for follow-up and tickets.

Context/why: trying to push latency down for small-chat use-case while keeping MRR/answer-quality within 3% of float16 baseline. Also investigating when KV cache warm-up beats recompute for short-turn dialogues.

Runs summary (3/11 - 3/13):
- run A (3/11): q4_0 static quant, no KV cache. batch=1, seq_in=128, seq_out=64. p95 lat=230ms, throughput=4.3 tok/s, perplexity gap +2.1% vs fp16 on eval prompts. Notes: occasional token collapse on longer generative prompts.
- run B (3/12): q4_1 dynamic per-layer, KV cache ON (prefix caching), batch=1. p95 lat=180ms, throughput=5.6 tok/s, quality delta +2.9% vs fp16. KV reduces repeated attention cost but increases memory by ~150MB.
- run C (3/13): q4_1 + small-kernel-tuning (fused matmul), KV ON, batch=2. p95 lat=200ms, throughput=10.1 tok/s per-GPU, quality delta +3.3%. Observed jitter in p95 when concurrent requests>8.

Quick observations:
- q4_1 gives better stability than q4_0 on generative traces (fewer degenerations).
- For short-turn dialogue (avg history 3 turns, 40 tokens/turn), warm KV cache gives net latency win after ~2 repeated turns. Cold-start penalty sometimes worse than recompute when sequence lengths vary widely.
- Batching helps throughput but complicates latency tail when autoscaler triggers cold warmups (see INF-1187).

Prompt stress tests (seed prompts):
- Role-play prompt with embedded json schema (90 tokens) -> quantized models sometimes hallucinate closing braces when using greedy decode. Temperature sweep shows higher temp increases hallucination rate for q4_0.
- Instruction-following: long-shot instructions (multi-step) show cumulative drift; add short anchor examples reduces drift by ~0.8% QA loss.

Quick commands / repro (local):
- start small: ./run_local.sh --model q4_1 --cache prefix --batch 1 --seq-in 128 --seq-out 64 --profile
- profile: python tools/profile_latency.py --tracefile /tmp/trace.json

Open questions / next steps:
- Can we reduce KV memory using pooling/sharding for short histories? (Q: tradeoffs vs additional latency from network fetch)
- Try mixed precision per-layer: keep FFNs in 8-bit, matmuls in 4-bit for critical layers (ticket: INF-1192).
- Build a small regression set for token-collapse cases — need 50 examples that reliably trigger collapse across seeds.
- Add A/B: q4_1 + cache vs fp16 no-cache under load (5–20 concurrent) to measure user-visible latency.

To-do (short):
- [ ] Add collapse regression set to repo (deadline: 3/20) — assigned to Ethan.
- [ ] Open PR with fused-kernel micro-optimizations (draft exists, see GH PR 432).
- [ ] Run mixed-precision per-layer sweep on 2 GPUs (no autoscale) — assigned to me.
- [ ] Write short note for SRE about memory delta when KV caches are enabled (numbers for Dedicated).

Notes to self / half-ideas:
- Maybe try prefix-only KV (store only last N tokens) to cap memory; empirical N=256 looks promising.
- When profiling, capture both device and host-side blocking times — hosts sometimes add 20–40ms when GPU kernels are short.

Links & refs:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/432
- Jira: INF-1187 (autoscale/coldstart tail)
- Slack notes: #aml-kv thread (search: "3/12 q4_1 warm-kv jitter")

Last quick log entry (3/13): strong candidate: q4_1 + small fused kernel + prefix-KV (N=256) — repeat with higher concurrency and add regression guard examples.

-- marta
